:::{#def-euclidean-norm}
#### Euclidean norm

The **Euclidean norm** (or *length*, also called the $L_2$ norm and written $\lVert \vx \rVert_2$) of a vector $\vx$ of length $p$ is

$$\norm{\vx} \eqdef \sqrt{\vx \cdot \vx} = \sqrt{\sumip x_i^2}$$ {#eq-l2-norm}

where $\sqrt{\cdot}$ is the [square root](algebra.qmd#def-square-root).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-euclidean-norm}
#### The length of a vector

For $\vx = (3, 4)$:

$$
\ba
\norm{\vx}
&= \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2}
&& \text{(definition of the norm)}
\\
&= \sqrt{25}
&& \text{(square and add)}
\\
&= 5
\ea
$$

The vector $(0.6, 0.8)$ has norm $\sqrt{0.36 + 0.64} = 1$.

:::
